I've been working this land for 35 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is familiar to me, the seasons are familiar. My thinking goes like this:

Cotton is my main money crop. I put 5 mu into cotton because that's been the backbone of my income for as long as I can remember. The other 5.9 mu I run as wheat in the winter and maize in the summer — same plots, two harvests. That's the standard rotation here and my neighbors all do it.

For cotton, I buy hybrid seed from the county seed station — the yields are better than what my father used to plant. Cotton needs a lot of attention: bollworm comes every year, aphids too, so I spray maybe six times. I pump the well five times through the season — once before flowering, again at boll set, and a few more times in the heat of summer. I rotary till before planting because the soil gets compacted after winter.

For wheat, I plant improved seed — not hybrid, just the improved variety the seed shop sells locally. I plough the field after maize comes off in September, then sow in October. I water four times: once before winter sets in to protect the roots, then at jointing, heading, and grain fill. Two pesticide runs — mainly herbicide early and maybe a fungicide if mildew shows up.

For summer maize after wheat harvest, I use hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or something similar, whatever the seed shop has that everyone else is using. I do rotary tillage right after wheat harvest and plant quickly. Three irrigations, two pesticide passes (herbicide at emergence and one for corn borer).

Some of my children work in town so I have less labor than before, but I've learned to work efficiently. I don't experiment much — I do what has fed this family for decades.
